reason: The agent only hardened json_array_append and added a NULL-charset fallback in json_string_set_cs; it did not touch Item_func_json_insert/json_remove, where a NULL path (s_p==NULL, e.g. 'x' % 'x') leaves c_path->p uninitialised while c_path->parsed is set, so the next evaluation calls json_find_path on garbage. The hidden test crashes the server (signal 11 in json_string_set_cs called from json_find_path <- Item_func_json_insert::val_str) on the json_insert query, so the crash the issue describes is still reachable for the sibling functions; the human fix adds 'else goto return_null' in json_insert/json_remove and guards all path functions.

The agent fixes the overrun by rejecting any byte sequence that is not valid utf8mb3 (len<=0 -> ER_WRONG_VALUE_FOR_VAR), while still receiving the value via val_str_ascii/latin1 and never converting the client charset to utf8mb3. As a result perfectly valid non-ASCII schema names cannot be set at all: the hidden test's first statement SET PATH _latin1 0xE5 fails with ER_WRONG_VALUE_FOR_VAR (and the error text shows an empty value ''), whereas the human fix converts the string to utf8mb3 and yields `å`. Although the issue only reports the crash, turning every non-ASCII PATH into an error is a functional regression a maintainer would reject, so W rather than A.

The agent adds an interval->with_param() check after fix_fields, which fixes the PREPARE '?' case (the first two hidden assertions pass) but leaves the identical crash for other non-constant items: the hidden test 'CREATE PROCEDURE p(v INT) CREATE TABLE ... INTERVAL v DAY' still kills the server ('Lost connection' instead of ER_PART_WRONG_VALUE) because an SP variable is also unbound at parse time and val_int() is still called on it. The human fix rejects any non-constant item via check_partition_func_processor before fix_fields. The remaining crash is a defect regardless of the tests, even though the issue text names only the '?' placeholder.

func_json_notembedded (the killability test the issue asks for: json_array_intersect and json_schema_valid returning ER_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT) passes with the agent's patch; only main.func_json fails. The diff is two extra 'Warning 4038 Syntax error in JSON text in argument 2' lines for json_array_intersect(@arr1, @obj1)/(@arr1, @num1), which come from the human fix additionally setting je2.s.error= JE_SYN when argument 2 is not an array, a side change the issue never mentions. The agent's code sets killed_ptr, adds JSON_DO_PAUSE_EXECUTION and reports JE_KILLED as requested, so the failure is a mismatch on an unspecified warning in the .result file.

The agent only guards mysql_lock_merge against a NULL save_lock in open_and_lock_internal_tables, which is equivalent to the first half of the human fix, but the hidden test still crashes with signal 11 at sql_table.cc:11023 (table->s->tmp_table after create_and_open_tmp_table). Under LOCK=EXCLUSIVE the TDC is flushed, so open_table() for the sequence takes the 'thd->open_tables->s->tdc->flushed' reopen path and closes the ALTER'd table, leaving 'table' dangling; the human fix adds '!table_list->sequence &&' to that condition. The agent's patch leaves the second crash cause from the issue (the close_tables_for_reopen assertion) unfixed.

The agent quotes the directory with append_unescaped(), which escapes a single quote by doubling it (DATA DIRECTORY='MYSQL_TMP_DIR/o''hara/'), while the human fix uses append_for_single_quote() producing o\'hara. Both are valid SQL string literals that re-create the table correctly; the issue only says the quote breaks SHOW CREATE TABLE and does not specify the escaping style. The hidden symlink.result fails solely on this exact-output difference ('' vs \').
